subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches inside plugin hook/skill and sandbox containment checks after the linked PR is repaired and proof is refreshed?
rationale: The performance fix is plausible and narrower than a process-wide cache, but it still changes cache reuse inside path-containment checks where stale canonical paths could matter.

options.title: Accept operation-scoped caches after repair
options.body: Fix the duplicate export/build failure, refresh proof on the current head, and accept per-operation cache lifetimes as the security/performance tradeoff.

options.title: Restrict caching to non-containment paths
options.body: Reject cache reuse in containment checks and pursue remaining performance wins only in plugin metadata or other non-boundary hot paths.

options.title: Pause for a cache-lifetime design
options.body: Hold the linked PR until maintainers define the exact cache scope and invalidation contract they want for these security-sensitive helpers.

recommendation.title: Accept operation-scoped caches after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the duplicate export/build failure, refresh proof on the current head, and accept per-operation cache lifetimes as the security/performance tradeoff.
